name: Mississippi
modelName: Percentage of the absent parent's adjusted gross income (Miss. Code § 43-19-101)
incomeLabel: Adjusted gross income: gross income minus the deductions the guideline allows.

statute.name: Miss. Code Ann. §§ 43-19-101, 43-19-103 (last amended by HB 1067, 2022 Reg. Sess., ch. 365, eff. July 1, 2022)

incomeDefinition: Gross income from all sources reasonably available to the absent parent (wages, self-employment, commissions, investments, trust income, his or her share of joint income, workers' compensation, disability, unemployment, annuity and retirement benefits including IRAs, any other payments, alimony, income from inherited property, any other earned income), excluding benefits derived from a second household such as a current spouse's income. Minus legally mandated deductions: federal, state and local taxes (actual liability only), Social Security contributions, and mandatory retirement and disability contributions. Minus support paid under an existing court order for other children, and optionally an amount the court deems appropriate for other children living with the parent. Annual total divided by 12 (§ 43-19-101(3)).
modelText: Monthly support = monthly adjusted gross income x 14% (1 child), 20% (2), 22% (3), 24% (4), 26% (5 or more) (§ 43-19-101(1), (3)). The guideline is a rebuttable presumption; deviation requires a written or on-record finding under the § 43-19-103 criteria (§ 43-19-101(2)).
sharedText: No shared-custody formula; a shared parental arrangement in which the noncustodial parent spends a great deal of time with the children is a criterion for deviating from the guideline (§ 43-19-103(g)).
addOnsText: Not a fixed add-on; the obligee's payment of child care to seek or keep employment is a deviation criterion (§ 43-19-103(i)). Every order must include reasonable medical support; the court makes findings on the availability and cost of health insurance, and if the custodial parent is required to obtain coverage its cost is taken into account in the award (§ 43-19-101(7) as renumbered in 2022). Extraordinary medical, psychological, educational or dental expenses are deviation criteria (§ 43-19-103(a)).
lowIncomeText: No self-support reserve or minimum order in the statute. Below $10,000 of annual adjusted gross income the court must make a written finding on whether the guideline is reasonable and take into account the basic subsistence needs of a parent with limited ability to pay; imputed income may not be a standard amount in lieu of fact-gathering (§ 43-19-101(4)-(5), as amended by HB 1067, 2022).

emancipation.text: Child support in Mississippi generally runs until the child reaches age 21, the age of majority (MDHS 2023 Quadrennial Review / Legislative task force report).

facts.text: Mississippi's percentages (14/20/22/24/26%) apply to income after taxes, Social Security and mandatory retirement contributions, which makes them lower in appearance than gross-income states (§ 43-19-101(3)).
Since July 1, 2022, imputed income may not be a standard amount in lieu of fact-gathering; it must rest on the parent's specific circumstances (§ 43-19-101(5), HB 1067).
Since July 1, 2023, courts may not treat incarceration as voluntary unemployment or underemployment when setting or modifying support (SB 2082, 2023, ch. 486).
MDHS must review the guidelines every four years; bills to switch to an income-shares model (HB 1552 in 2025, HB 980 in 2026) died in the Legislature.
Parents may request a review of the support amount every three years through MDHS (MDHS Child Support).
